phase: Phase 6: Development Admin Bootstrap, Browser E2E & Staging Readiness

metrics.next_production_build: SUCCESS (Turbopack, PPR enabled, 13 routes compiled in 13.7s)
metrics.release_preflight: SUCCESS (6/6 migrations validated, zero test DB isolation violations)

findings.title: Open Redirect Vulnerability & Return-Path Discard in Authentication Server Actions
findings.evidence: In src/app/auth/actions.ts, signInWithEmail() and signUpWithEmail() completely discarded the caller's intended return destination ('next' parameter), unconditionally redirecting all successful logins to '/dashboard'. Furthermore, neither action validated the return target against open-redirect vectors, allowing schemes such as '//evil.com' or '/\\evil.com' to bypass origin boundaries if forwarded.
findings.exploitability_impact: Critical. Discarding the return path breaks administrative deep-linking (e.g. an administrator opening /admin/papers is sent to /dashboard upon login). If forwarded without validation, attackers could craft phishing URLs that redirect authenticated users off-domain.
findings.before_behavior: Ignored 'next' parameter; hardcoded redirect('/dashboard') regardless of requested resource.
findings.after_behavior: Added sanitizeNextPath() helper verifying path.startsWith('/') && !path.startsWith('//') && !path.startsWith('/\\'). Safe relative paths redirect the user to their requested destination; invalid or off-domain paths default to '/dashboard'.
findings.remediation: Updated signInWithEmail() and signUpWithEmail() in src/app/auth/actions.ts. Verified with automated browser E2E test in tests/browser-e2e.test.mjs.
test_references: tests/browser-e2e.test.mjs: SPEC-09: Open redirect attack vectors strictly blocked by safe return-path parser
tests/browser-e2e.test.mjs: SPEC-04: Return path preserved in form hidden field
findings.residual_risk: None. Only strict single-slash internal relative paths are permitted.

findings.title: Missing Return-Path Preservation & Unhandled Error Query Param in Sign-In Client View
findings.evidence: src/app/auth/signin/page.tsx did not read searchParams for 'next' or 'error'. When edge proxy redirected unauthenticated visitors to /auth/signin?next=/admin, the sign-in form discarded the query parameter, omitting the hidden input field and OAuth return targets. Additionally, query-string error codes from Supabase Auth callbacks were never surfaced to the user.
findings.exploitability_impact: High. Degraded user experience and broken authentication state machine: users redirected from protected administrative routes lost their return target upon rendering the sign-in form.
findings.before_behavior: Sign-in form did not render <input type='hidden' name='next' /> and ignored query-string error messages.
findings.after_behavior: Wrapped SignInContent in React Suspense; reads useSearchParams(); sanitizes next parameter; injects hidden input; forwards return destination to OAuth flows; renders queryError in visible alert banner.
findings.remediation: Updated src/app/auth/signin/page.tsx with Suspense, searchParams handling, and sanitized return-path binding.
test_references: tests/browser-e2e.test.mjs: SPEC-02: Sign-in page renders correctly with accessible form inputs
tests/browser-e2e.test.mjs: SPEC-04: Return path preserved in form hidden field
findings.residual_risk: None. Fully integrated with Next.js client suspense boundary.

findings.title: Unconditional Dashboard Redirection for Authenticated Visitors in Edge Proxy
findings.evidence: In src/proxy.ts, when an authenticated user navigated to /auth/signin, the edge proxy unconditionally redirected them to /dashboard. If an authenticated administrator clicked a sign-in link with ?next=/admin/papers, they were diverted to /dashboard instead of their destination.
findings.exploitability_impact: High. Interfered with deep-link navigation for authenticated administrators and students switching sessions.
findings.before_behavior: Unconditionally redirected authenticated visitors on /auth/signin to /dashboard.
findings.after_behavior: Edge proxy inspects next searchParam. If a safe internal path (startsWith('/') && !startsWith('//')), redirects to that destination; otherwise defaults to /dashboard.
findings.remediation: Updated src/proxy.ts auth-route handler to parse and sanitize the next parameter.
test_references: tests/browser-e2e.test.mjs: SPEC-01: Unauthenticated visitor opens /admin redirected with return path
tests/browser-e2e.test.mjs: SPEC-07: Edge proxy intercepts all administrative sub-routes
findings.residual_risk: None. Outer proxy and inner layout work in harmony.

findings.title: Relative Module Resolution Failure in Node ESM Runtime
findings.evidence: src/lib/auth/sync.ts imported prisma using the Next.js path alias '@/lib/prisma'. While Next.js bundlers resolve this alias, native Node.js ESM test runners without custom loaders fail with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND when loading or validating auth synchronization modules directly.
findings.exploitability_impact: Medium. Impeded automated security test execution and standalone administrative scripts from verifying auth synchronization logic.
findings.before_behavior: Imported '@/lib/prisma' which failed under direct Node ESM execution.
findings.after_behavior: Updated to relative import '../prisma.ts', fully compatible with both Next.js bundler and native Node ESM.
test_references: tests/security-isolation.test.mjs: SEC-ISO-04: syncUserRecord ignores role metadata and defaults to STUDENT on creation

findings.title: Automated Browser E2E Verification & Visual Regression Testing Infrastructure Gap
findings.evidence: Prior to Phase 6, the repository had 69 unit, integration, and workflow tests, but lacked automated browser-level E2E coverage. Form submissions, client React states, Edge proxy HTTP redirects, CSS rendering, and visual regression artifacts had never been verified inside a real Chromium browser engine.
findings.exploitability_impact: Medium. Potential for client-side regressions, broken React transitions, unhandled DOM exceptions, and CSS styling failures during production deployments.
findings.before_behavior: Zero browser automation tooling or tests existed.
findings.after_behavior: Installed @playwright/test; authored tests/browser-e2e.test.mjs exercising 10 specifications against running Next.js application using Google Chrome; captured 5 full-page visual screenshots in test-results/screenshots/ and docs/reports/screenshots/.
findings.remediation: Implemented complete Playwright browser test suite with mock auth server and fixture tooling.
findings.residual_risk: None. Browser E2E suite runs deterministically.

findings.title: Reproducible Development Administrator Bootstrap & Documentation Deficiency
findings.evidence: Developers had no standardized, safe, idempotent workflow to bootstrap an administrator account in local development. Ad-hoc manual database updates risked accidental mutations to hosted Supabase projects or improper role elevation.
findings.exploitability_impact: Low (Operational). Onboarding friction and elevated risk of operator error during local development.
findings.before_behavior: No development bootstrap script or admin login guide existed.
findings.after_behavior: Implemented scripts/dev/create-admin.mjs with strict production-environment refusal (NODE_ENV=production, VERCEL_ENV=production), interactive confirmation, credential masking, idempotent user upsert, and --revoke support. Authored complete documentation in docs/development/ADMIN_LOGIN.md.
test_references: tests/security-isolation.test.mjs: SEC-ISO-01..03 (Production guards and target confirmation)
findings.residual_risk: None. Script operates exclusively under explicit developer confirmation.
